anomalies.observed: The netlist places all VDD, VDDA, VREF+, VBAT, and VCAP pins of FCC2 and NAVC2 on unconnected nets (or on VDDA_NAVC which only connects to a decoupling capacitor C5).
anomalies.expected: These pins should be connected to the 3.3V rail (+3V3 or +3.3V) as required by the STM32 datasheets and the specification.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: The MCUs receive no core or analog power, so the board cannot boot or function.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address pin A0 (pin 1) is connected to the +3.3V rail, while A1-A5 are grounded.
anomalies.expected: For I2C address 0x40, all address pins A0-A5 must be tied to GND.
anomalies.impact: The PCA9685 responds at I2C address 0x41 instead of 0x40, so software expecting 0x40 will fail to control the PWM/servo outputs.

anomalies.observed: The netlist contains no component with value or part CH330, despite the specification calling for two otter_CH330 USB-UART bridges on the Connections sheet.
anomalies.expected: Two CH330 USB-UART bridge ICs should be present in the Connections sheet.
anomalies.impact: The board lacks the intended USB-to-UART programming/debug interfaces, preventing serial communication with the MCUs over USB.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple serious anomalies: the STM32 MCUs have unconnected power pins, the PCA9685 PWM driver is configured for I2C address 0x41 instead of 0x40, and the two specified CH330 USB-UART bridges are missing. These deviations would prevent the board from powering up, communicating with the servo driver, and providing USB serial debug.
